SELECT *

🔍 Query Breakdown
Line 1: SELECT *
- SELECT tells the database that you want to retrieve data.
- * (asterisk) means all columns.

Line 2: FROM table_name;
FROM tells SQL where the data is stored. Here, table_name is the table name.

⚙️ SQL Execution Order:
Step 1: FROM table_name (Locate the specified table)
Step 2: SELECT * (Retrieve every column from every row)

Execution Flow:
table_name ──► Read every row ──► Read every column ──► Display result

🚀 Alternative Solutions:
Method 1 (Recommended):
```sql
SELECT *
FROM table_name;
```

Method 2 (Explicit Column Names):
```sql
SELECT column1, column2, column3
FROM table_name;
```

⚡ Performance Notes:
SELECT * retrieves all columns, good for learning/debugging. In production, requesting only needed columns saves memory and bandwidth.

Step 2: SELECT columns (Retrieve only the specified columns)

employees table ──► Read every row ──► Pick only specified columns ──► Display Result

🚀 Alternative Solutions:

⚡ Performance Notes:
Method 1 reads only required columns, making it faster and preferred in production. Method 2 retrieves unnecessary columns, increasing memory and network usage.
